facts.text: China RatingDog services PMI Dec 52.0 vs consensus 52.0 (Nov 52.1).

PAP week-ahead: Reuters poll saw Dec payrolls +55k (Nov +64k, unemployment 4.6%); Trump said he would name Powell's successor in January (Powell's chair term ends May) and renewed threats to sue Powell over the HQ renovation; EZ Dec HICP expected 2.0% (Nov 2.1%).
10Y closes 2 Jan (Bloomberg generic via PAP): Bund 2.90%, OAT 3.61%, BTP 3.61%, Bonos 3.34%, gilt 4.54% -> OAT-Bund and BTP-Bund both ~71bp, Spain ~44bp.

Mid-session 5 Jan: UST 10Y 4.18% (-1bp), 30Y 4.87%, 2s10s +71bp; Bund 10Y 2.88% (-2bp); DXY 98.77 (+0.34%), EUR/USD 1.1663; Brent Mar $61.33 (+0.9%); gold/silver up after the 3 Jan US operation in Venezuela.
US ISM manufacturing Dec 47.9 vs consensus 48.4 (Nov 48.2), still below 50.

Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari (CNBC, 5 Jan): inflation slowly trending down but risk is persistence from tariffs; unemployment (~4.6%) could 'pop' higher; policy roughly neutral; no oil-price effect yet from Venezuela.

Venezuela: Maduro and his wife pleaded not guilty to four narco-terrorism/cocaine counts in a New York federal court on 5 Jan (next hearing 17 Mar); Delcy Rodriguez sworn in as acting president; Rubio said the US naval blockade stays until US demands (incl. oil-sector access) are met.

OPEC+ kept oil output unchanged at a brief meeting on 4 Jan; Pekao economists said the Venezuela operation had no significant market impact and any extra Venezuelan supply would need large investment.

Trump said a bill on Russia sanctions and tariffs on buyers of Russian oil would soon pass Congress; Trump reiterated the US 'absolutely needs' Greenland, Danish PM said he is seriously considering it.

Wall Street closed higher 5 Jan with the Dow at a record; Exxon/Chevron/oil services rallied on Trump's plans to revive Venezuela's oil industry; gold futures ~+3%; investors judged the Venezuela events too small to derail markets.
China tightened export controls on dual-use goods to Japan (6 Jan) over PM Takaichi's Taiwan remarks.
France flash CPI Dec 0.8% y/y (cons 0.9%), HICP 0.7% y/y (cons 0.8%); energy -6.8% y/y.
Final services PMIs Dec: euro area 52.4 (flash 52.6, Nov 53.6), composite 51.5 (flash 51.9); Germany services 52.7 (flash 52.6); France 50.1 (flash 50.2); UK services 51.4 (flash 52.1).
JPMorgan: France, Belgium and Austria are the euro-area members most vulnerable to rating downgrades in 2026 (~50% chance each).
German flash CPI Dec 1.8% y/y (Nov 2.3%), HICP 2.0% y/y (Nov 2.6%), both a steeper fall than expected (PAP cited a 2.0% consensus but labelled the 1.8% CPI figure 'HICP').

Richmond Fed's Barkin (6 Jan): rates now within the range of neutral estimates after 75bp of 2025 easing; future moves need 'finely tuned judgments' balancing an edging-up jobless rate and above-target inflation.
US S&P Global services PMI final Dec 52.5 (flash 52.9, Nov 54.1); composite 52.7 (flash 53.0, Nov 54.2).
US Supreme Court set Friday 9 Jan as an opinion day with the IEEPA tariff case pending.

6 Jan: UST 10Y 4.185% (+2bp); Bund 10Y 2.84% (-3bp) after soft German inflation; EUR/USD 1.1687; silver +5% to $80.65, gold $4,497; Brent Mar $61.53 (-0.4%) at 17:59, Feb-labelled Brent $60.60 (-1.9%) at 22:09; Dow and S&P 500 at records.
Fed Governor Miran (Fox Business, 6 Jan): policy 'clearly restrictive', 'well over 100 basis points of cuts' justified in 2026; target range 3.50-3.75%; markets expected a hold in January.

Ukraine: Paris 'coalition of the willing' summit (6 Jan) adopted the Paris Declaration on security guarantees; UK/France pledged troops after a ceasefire; Macron said ceasefire monitoring would be US-led; Witkoff said security protocols 'largely finalised'; Zelensky called it a 'big step forward'.

Greenland: White House aide Stephen Miller questioned Danish sovereignty and would not rule out force; EU does not recognise Delcy Rodriguez's mandate; French PM Lecornu called the Maduro capture illegal.

Trump (Truth Social, evening 6 Jan ET): Venezuela's interim authorities will turn over 30-50m barrels of sanctioned oil to be sold at market price with proceeds controlled by him; Energy Secretary Wright (7 Jan) said sales would continue indefinitely; oil fell.
Czech flash CPI Dec 2.1% y/y, -0.3% m/m (final due 13 Jan).
Germany: unemployment rate Dec 6.3% (cons 6.3%); retail sales Nov -0.6% m/m (cons +0.2%; Oct revised +0.3%).
Euro area flash HICP Dec 2.0% y/y (Reuters poll 2.0%, Nov 2.1%); core 2.3% (Nov 2.4%, lowest since Aug); services 3.4% (3.5%); energy -1.9%; Italy 1.2%, Spain 3.0%, France 0.7%, Germany 2.0%.
After the flash HICP, markets expect the ECB to keep its 2% deposit rate unchanged through 2026 (next meeting 5 Feb).
ADP Dec private payrolls +41k vs +50k expected (Nov revised -29k).
JOLTS Nov job openings 7.146m vs 7.648m expected (Oct revised 7.449m).
ISM services Dec 54.4 vs 52.2 expected (Nov 52.6); durable goods Oct final -2.2% m/m.

Polish strategist (PAP FX/FI): Australian and euro-area inflation surprised lower (EZ core 2.3%), supporting core bonds; soft US labour data would raise Fed-cut expectations and push EUR/USD toward 1.18.
7 Jan: UST 10Y 4.14% (-3bp), 30Y 4.82% (-5bp), 2s10s +68bp; Bund 10Y 2.81% (-3bp); DXY 98.65; Brent Mar $60.81 (-0.9%) at 18:08 (~$60.30 at 22:17); Stoxx 600 Energy -3% on Venezuela oil plans.
Trump called for a $1.5tn FY2027 military budget (vs $901bn approved for 2026), citing tariff revenue.
German factory orders Nov +5.6% m/m vs -1.0% expected (Oct revised +1.6%).
Euro area: unemployment Nov 6.3% (Oct 6.4%); ESI Dec 96.7 vs 97.1 expected; PPI Nov +0.5% m/m (cons +0.4%), -1.7% y/y (cons -1.7%).
ECB VP de Guindos (8 Jan): interest rates are at an appropriate level, but uncertainty from geopolitical events is 'enormous'.
US initial jobless claims 208k vs 212k expected (prior 200k); continuing claims 1.914m; Oct trade deficit $29.4bn (Sep revised $48.1bn); Challenger Dec layoffs -8.3% y/y.
PAP/Reuters: markets expect the Fed to cut at least twice by 25bp in 2026 ahead of Friday payrolls; Treasury rally paused as layoffs fell to a 17-month low.
Fed Governor Miran (Bloomberg TV, 8 Jan): looking for about 150bp of rate cuts in 2026 to support the cooling labour market (Dec dot-plot median: one cut).

PAP FX/FI (mBank's Sutowicz): Friday brings payrolls and a possible Supreme Court tariff ruling; striking down IEEPA tariffs would be positive for the dollar; CZK and HUF weakened slightly in early 2026.

Russia's foreign ministry (Zakharova) rejected the Paris plan: Western troops deployed in Ukraine after a ceasefire would be 'legitimate military targets'; Ukraine and backers dubbed an 'axis of war'.

Treasury Secretary Bessent (8 Jan): Trump will pick the next Fed chair this month; one of four finalists (BlackRock's Rieder) still to be interviewed; Hassett and Warsh seen as front-runners, Waller also interviewed.
8 Jan: UST 10Y 4.17% (+3bp) as the global bond rally stalled; Bund 10Y ~2.84% (+3bp at 14:34); EUR/USD ~1.1655; Brent Mar $61.16 (+2%) at 18:18; defence stocks surged on the $1.5tn budget call.

Brent settled $61.99 (+$2.03, +3.4%), WTI $57.76 (+3.2%) on 8 Jan on supply worries (Iran unrest/internet blackout, Iraq West Qurna 2, Black Sea tanker attack, US Russia-sanctions bill) after two days of falls.

Trump (Truth Social, 8 Jan US afternoon) directed 'representatives' (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac) to buy $200bn of mortgage bonds to lower mortgage rates; MBS outperformed Treasuries (PAP report 9 Jan 07:53).
China CPI Dec +0.8% y/y (in line; highest since Mar 2023), PPI -1.9% y/y (Nov -2.2%); 2025 CPI flat, PPI -2.6%.
Closes 8 Jan (Bloomberg generic via PAP): Bund 10Y 2.86% (+5bp vs 2.81% on 7 Jan), OAT 3.53%, BTP 3.51%, Bonos 3.26%, gilt 4.40%, UST 10Y 4.18% -> OAT-Bund 67bp, BTP-Bund 65bp.
Germany Nov industrial production +0.8% m/m vs -0.7% expected (Oct revised +2.0%); exports -2.5% m/m; France IP -0.1% m/m; euro-area retail sales Nov +0.2% m/m (cons +0.1%).
Russia fired an Oreshnik hypersonic missile at the Lviv region overnight 8-9 Jan, after rejecting Western peacekeepers; Ukraine urged allies to raise pressure.

CNB minutes of 18 Dec meeting (released 9 Jan): unanimous 6-0 hold at 3.50%; Michl: all options on the rate path open; Frait: rates equally likely to move either way; Seidler: moderately restrictive policy desirable.

Trump (Fox/NYT, 8 Jan): backs the bipartisan Russia-sanctions bill (penalising buyers of Russian oil incl. China/India) but hopes not to use it; threatened to strike Iran if protesters are killed; Brent Mar $62.67 (+1.1%).

US Dec payrolls +50k vs Dow Jones est. 73k (PAP: 70k); Nov revised to 56k (from 64k), Oct -173k (from -105k), two-month revision -76k; unemployment 4.4% vs 4.5% expected; AHE +0.3% m/m, 3.8% y/y (0.2pp above expectations).
UMich sentiment Jan prelim 54.0 vs 53.5 expected (Dec 52.9); 1y inflation expectations 4.2% (cons 4.1%), 5-10y 3.4% (cons 3.3%, prior 3.2%); housing starts Oct 1.246m, permits 1.412m (cons 1.35m).
US Supreme Court issued opinions on 9 Jan but no ruling on IEEPA tariffs; next opinion day set for Wednesday 14 Jan.
EU member states gave provisional approval (9 Jan) to sign the EU-Mercosur free-trade deal over French opposition; signing planned for the following week.
9 Jan (18:15): UST 10Y 4.17% (-1bp), 30Y 4.83%; USD firmer, EUR/USD 1.163; Brent Mar $63.9 (+3%); European indices up, miners led on Rio Tinto-Glencore talks; S&P 500 then closed at a record (22:13).
Analysts read payrolls as supporting a Fed hold at the late-January meeting; markets still priced at least two 2026 cuts vs one in the Dec dots.

France: National Assembly finance committee rejected the revenue part (9 Jan) and spending part (10 Jan) of the 2026 budget in new reading; plenary debate runs 13-23 Jan; lawmakers expect Lecornu may need Article 49.3.

Weekend: Trump signed an order (9 Jan) ring-fencing Venezuelan oil revenue in Treasury accounts and said oil firms will invest at least $100bn; Iran protests (>=2,000 dead per Iran International), WSJ: Trump to review strike/sanction/cyber options on Tuesday; Trump called for a one-year 10% cap on credit-card rates from 20 Jan.

Powell video statement (Sun 11 Jan, 7:30pm ET): DOJ served the Fed grand-jury subpoenas threatening criminal indictment over his June Senate testimony on the HQ renovation; Powell called it a pretext stemming from the Fed setting rates by its own assessment and vowed to continue.

Sen. Tillis (R, Banking Committee) said he will oppose any Fed nominee, including the chair, until the DOJ matter is resolved; Warren backed blocking votes; Trump told NBC he knew nothing of the probe; JPMorgan now expects the Fed on hold through 2026.
ING (Knightley, PAP week-ahead): Dec CPI will not materially change pricing of at least two 25bp Fed cuts in H2 2026; market expects no change at 27-28 Jan FOMC.

Closes 9 Jan (Bloomberg generic via PAP): Bund 10Y 2.86%, OAT 3.52%, BTP 3.50%, Bonos 3.25%, gilt 4.37% -> OAT-Bund 66bp, BTP-Bund 64bp, Spain 39bp (France wider than Italy); gilt -17bp since 2 Jan; UST 2Y 3.53% (from 3.49% on 8 Jan, i.e. +4bp on payrolls day), UST 10Y 4.17%.
Sentix investor confidence Jan -1.8 vs -4.9 expected (Dec -6.2).
MNB Governor Varga (12 Jan, BSE press conference): EUR/HUF ~385 vs ~410 a year earlier, 'saving in HUF paid off'; reserves above EUR 50bn; no new rate guidance.

'Sell America' on 12 Jan after the Powell news: DXY 98.78 (-0.36%), EUR/USD 1.1683, GBP 1.3465; long-end UST yields jumped, 10Y 4.20% (+3bp); Bund 10Y 2.82% (-1bp); gold record ~$4,577 (+1.5%); US equity futures down.

ECB's Villeroy (Banque de France New Year address, 12 Jan): a 2026 ECB rate hike is a 'fanciful theory' barring an unlikely shock; ECB to stay pragmatic and agile; dollar could fall if Fed independence is threatened.
12 Jan close: S&P 500/Dow records despite the Powell probe; bank/card stocks fell on Trump's 10% credit-card cap call; Brent ~$63.8 (+0.8%) at 22:18.
Trump (Truth Social, 12 Jan): any country doing business with Iran faces a 25% tariff on trade with the US, 'effective immediately' (no implementation details).

NY Fed's Williams (CFR, evening 12 Jan ET): policy 'well positioned' after 75bp of cuts; inflation to peak ~2.75-3% in H1 2026, just under 2.5% for 2026, 2% in 2027; unemployment to stabilise; GDP 2.5-2.75%; data dependent.
Japan: Nikkei +3.1% to a record and the yen weakest vs USD since July 2024 on speculation PM Takaichi will call a snap election; regional bond prices slipped.

Hungary CPI Dec 3.3% y/y (Nov 3.8%; matched Portfolio poll), 0.1% m/m; core 3.8% (4.1%); services 6.8%. MNB: data above its December Inflation Report projection; no rate change in January, will watch early-year services repricing.
Czech CPI Dec final 2.1% y/y (Nov 2.1%), HICP 1.8%; CNB: close to its 2.3% forecast.
Heads of ECB, BoE, BoC and other central banks plus BIS issued a joint statement of 'full solidarity' with Powell and Fed independence (BoJ did not sign).
US CPI Dec +0.3% m/m, 2.7% y/y (both in line); core +0.2% m/m, 2.6% y/y vs 0.3%/2.7% expected (Nov core 2.6%).
NFIB small-business optimism Dec 99.5 (cons 99.2); new home sales Oct 737k (cons 715k).
St Louis Fed's Musalem (MNI webcast, 13 Jan): CPI encouraging but 'little reason' for near-term easing; policy near neutral; inflation closer to 3% than 2%, should ebb; growth at/above potential.
13 Jan: UST 10Y 4.18%, 2s10s +65bp; Bund 10Y 2.85%; DXY 99.16 (+0.3%), EUR/USD 1.1646; Brent Mar $65.66 (+2.8%) at 18:06 (settled ~+2.5%, highest since Nov) on Iran tariff threat; silver $88.69.
Venezuela's PDVSA restarting wells and exports resuming (Reuters); four tankers attacked near the CPC terminal in the Black Sea (Bloomberg).
Bloomberg: Treasuries rallied after soft core CPI; swaps almost fully price a Fed cut by the June meeting, minimal odds for 28 Jan.
China Dec exports +6.6% y/y vs 3.0% Reuters poll (Nov 5.9%); imports +5.7% vs 0.9%; 2025 trade surplus a record $1.189tn.
10Y closes 13 Jan (Bloomberg generic via PAP): Bund 2.85%, OAT 3.52% (+67bp), BTP 3.48% (+63bp), Bonos 3.24% (+39bp), gilt 4.40%; UST 10Y 4.17% at 06:32.

BoE MPC member Taylor (Singapore, 14 Jan): inflation can be at target by mid-2026 rather than 2027; Bank Rate (3.75%) should reach neutral 'sooner rather than later'; markets close to pricing two more BoE cuts in 2026.

ECB VP de Guindos (Madrid, 14 Jan): inflation (2.0% in Dec) should stabilise at 2% medium term; 2026 growth revised above 1%; geopolitics raises downside growth risks; financial-stability risks elevated with stretched valuations and fiscal concerns.
Brent Mar $66.20 (+1.1%) at 13:17, fifth straight gain; Brent +9% over the previous four sessions on Iran unrest/US strike risk (Iran output ~3.3m b/d).
US retail sales Nov +0.6% m/m (PAP: cons 0.5%; control group +0.4%); PPI Nov +0.2% m/m (cons ~0.3%), 3.0% y/y; existing home sales Dec 4.35m (cons 4.22m); MBA applications +28.5%.
Supreme Court again issued no IEEPA tariff ruling on 14 Jan; decision delayed to at least the following week.

Greenland: Denmark/Greenland FMs met Vance and Rubio at the White House; Danish FM Rasmussen cited a 'fundamental disagreement' but a high-level working group will be formed; Trump reiterated 'we need Greenland'.
14 Jan: UST 10Y 4.13% (-5bp), 30Y 4.79%, 2s10s +62bp; Bund 10Y 2.81% (-3bp); DXY 98.98; silver record ~$91 (+5.6%), gold $4,624; US equities fell a second day.
Ukraine declared an energy state of emergency after massive Russian strikes left Kyiv short of power, heat and water.
Brent Mar settled $66.52 (+$1.05, +1.6%; high $66.67, ~3-month high), WTI $62.90, then fell ~1.9% after settlement when Trump said the 'killing in Iran is stopping'; US crude stocks +3.3m bbl.

Fedspeak 14 Jan: Kashkari 'way too soon' to cut, wants a January hold, defended Powell; Philadelphia's Paulson sees cuts later in 2026 if forecasts hold, policy 'a little restrictive'; Bostic: inflation fight 'not won', policy should stay restrictive; Miran: deregulation another reason to cut. Recap pricing: Jan cut ~9%, March ~26%, April ~60%.

Iran: some personnel told to leave Al Udeid base in Qatar; Reuters: US intervention possible within 24 hours; Trump later suggested he may hold off if executions of protesters stop; Citi raised its 3-month Brent forecast to $70.

fed_pricing.text: CME FedWatch: 82.8% hold / 17.2% 25bp cut at 28 Jan FOMC; by March 49.4% unchanged, 43.6% cumulative -25bp, 6.9% -50bp (BlockBeats via KuCoin; 23:45 UTC+8).
Euro area: markets expect ECB deposit rate held at 2% through all of 2026.
US: markets expect at least two 25bp Fed cuts in 2026 (vs one in Dec dots); soft US data also pushed back the timing of the first priced ECB hike (PAP 8 Jan 08:28/09:48).
CME FedWatch pre-payrolls: Jan cut 11.6% (hold 88.4%); by March cumulative -25bp 35.8%, -50bp 3.7%, unchanged 60.6% (Odaily 21:29 UTC+8).
CME FedWatch post-payrolls: Jan cut 2.8% (hold 97.2%); by March -25bp 32.3%, -50bp 0.9%, unchanged 66.8% (Odaily 21:57 UTC+8). CNBC: next cut not fully priced until June.
ING: market prices at least two 25bp Fed cuts in H2 2026; no change expected at 27-28 Jan FOMC.
After the Powell subpoena: JPMorgan economists now expect the Fed on hold throughout 2026; before the news markets expected 'one, perhaps two' cuts in 2026.
CME FedWatch pre-CPI: Jan cut 5.0% (hold 95.0%); by March -25bp 24.3%, -50bp 1.1%, unchanged 74.6% (Odaily 21:16 UTC+8).
Post-CPI swaps almost fully price a Fed cut by the June meeting; minimal odds for 28 Jan (Bloomberg).
BoE: investors close to pricing two further 25bp BoE cuts in 2026 (Bank Rate 3.75%).
CME FedWatch: Jan cut 5% (hold 95%); by March -25bp 26%, -50bp 1.2%, unchanged 72.8% (Odaily via KuCoin, 23:16 UTC+8).
investingLive Fedspeak recap: Jan cut ~9%, March ~26%, April ~60% (different source/method than FedWatch).
